amendments.rule: A generic Greek article the ASV renders by the **indefinite** determiner is `aligned` to that determiner, headed on it. Rule 19 names only *the* because that is the ordinary case, and rule 23's `unrepresented` is for an article English realizes nowhere — not for one the ASV realizes with *a* or *an*. `ὁ κόκκος τοῦ σίτου` → *a grain of wheat*, `τὸν ἄνθρωπον` → *a man*, `τὸ ψεῦδος` → *a lie*, and `τὸ πρόσωπον` → *a face* all give the indefinite to the article. The test is whether the determiner is the article's own to take. Where the Greek is anarthrous there is no article to compete and the supplied determiner is an ordinary rule 7 helper on the word it determines — `φῶς` → *a light*, `κλέπτης` → *a thief*, `δεῖπνον` → *a supper*, and the substantival `νεκρῶν` → *the dead* — and where another source word already occupies the determiner slot, rules 20, 38 and 49 empty the article exactly as they do before *the*. A **distributive `κατά`** is such a word. The distribution is what the preposition contributes and no other token carries it, so where the ASV renders the distributive by *every* that determiner is the preposition's own and an article governing the noun is its own `unrepresented` unit under rule 23: `κατὰ τὰς συναγωγάς` → *in every synagogue* gives *in every* to `κατά` and nothing to the article, as `κατὰ τοὺς οἴκους` → *every house* does at ACT.8.3. Rule 17 heads such a unit on the word realizing the preposition where the ASV writes one — *in every* on *in* at ACT.14.23, ACT.15.21, ACT.20.23 and TIT.1.5, and *of every* on *of* at LUK.8.4 — and on *every* itself where it writes none, as ACT.8.3, LUK.2.41 and JHN.21.25 do. The corpus is eight units to none and not one of them reads the determiner off the article, so this is not a judgment call; do not split *in every* or *of every* across the preposition and the article, and do not leave the preposition `unrepresented` in order to give *every* to the noun's article. Where no preposition competes the ordinary reading holds and a supplied *every* is the article's own to take, as `τὰς ἡμέρας` → *every day* and `τὰς νύκτας` → *every night* are at LUK.21.37. So a definite-to-indefinite shift in the ASV is not evidence that the article realizes nothing, and it is not a licence to read a determiner off the article where the Greek never had one.
amendments.why: Rule 51 already states the governing test — whether the supplied determiner is the article's own to take — and enumerates the displacers that empty it (rules 20, 38, 49). A distributive κατά is a fourth displacer the rule had not considered, and the evidence round settled it: all 8 corpus units of κατά rendered *every* or *in every* align the determiner to the preposition, the head standing on the prepositional word where the ASV writes one and on *every* where it does not, and the one arthrous parallel (ACT.8.3) does not align its article to *every*, since the LEMMA=ὁ TARGET=every query returns only LUK.21.37, where no preposition stands. Amending rule 51 rather than adding a new rule keeps the determiner test in one place; without it a later pass reading rule 51's own list would find nothing forbidding a *the*-less article from claiming the *every*, which is the reading ACT.22.19's note had to argue against.

conventions: Where the ASV compresses an appositional ἀνήρ into the single English word rendering the noun standing with it, ἀνήρ is its own `unrepresented` unit under rules 23 and 39's test: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί → *Brethren* at 22:1 and ἀνὴρ Ἰουδαῖος → *a Jew* at 22:3 give the whole word to ἀδελφοί and to Ἰουδαῖος. Where the ASV writes *man* for it the ordinary alignment holds, as ἀνὴρ εὐλαβής → *a devout man* does at 22:12 with the supplied determiner on the noun under rule 58. Joining the two tokens on the single word remains defensible and is named in each unit's note; a reference comparison reports the empty ἀνήρ as a disagreement.

A periphrastic εἰμί is decided by the English the ASV wrote. Where the ASV keeps the periphrasis, the copula or auxiliary is the verb's own `aligned` unit — ἤμην ἐφεστώς → *was standing by* at 22:20, ἦν δεδεκώς → *he had bound* at 22:29, where *had* is the only word answering to it. Where the ASV collapses the periphrasis into a simple past, nothing is left for the copula and it is its own `unrepresented` unit: ἤμην φυλακίζων καὶ δέρων → *I imprisoned and beat* at 22:19, the copula there governing two participles at once so that no one of them can carry it. Folding it onto the first participle remains defensible and is named in that unit's note; a reference comparison reports the empty ἤμην as a disagreement.

report: Checked all 55 candidate lemma groups end to end, and read the dump for the added-versus-folded split the candidate table is blind to. No construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source licensing the difference, so patches is empty.

ὁ (70 occurrences): every unrepresented article has a stated displacer — attributive demonstrative (22:3, 22:4, 22:11, 22:22, 22:26, 22:28), genitive possessive (22:14 x3, 22:16 x2, 22:20, 22:22), article before a name (22:3, 22:6, 22:8, 22:25, 22:28, 22:30), determinerless genitive under rule 21 (22:3), nominalizing article (22:30), distributive κατά (22:19). 22:23 τὰ ἱμάτια to 'their' under rule 20's second arm and 22:22 τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν with the article empty are the two arms of one test, divided by whether a genitive pronoun stands. 22:14 τὸν δίκαιον to 'the … One' / 'Righteous' (rule 102) and 22:30 τὸ ἀσφαλές to 'the' / 'certainty' differ because 'certainty' glosses the lexeme and 'One' does not, which is rule 102's own test.

Supplied words are placed uniformly: complementizer 'that' on the non-finite complement (22:6, 22:17, 22:22, 22:24, rule 85); subordinator when/as/while on the participle (22:2, 22:6, 22:17, 22:23, 22:26, 22:29, rule 86); coordinating juncture on the verb it introduces (22:5, 22:10, 22:16, 22:22, 22:26, 22:27, 22:30, rule 88), with 22:10 and 22:16 rendering the identical ἀναστάς-plus-imperative frame identically; a subject pronoun on the participle only where the Greek leaves the subject unexpressed, and on the expressed dative or genitive where it does not (22:5, 22:6, 22:17, 22:23, 22:26, 22:29, rule 74).

Rule 106 is applied in all three arms without conflict: preverb particle inside the verb's unit (22:3, 22:13, 22:16 twice, 22:20, 22:21, 22:22, 22:30 twice); an expressed preposition taking the whole prepositional expression while the verb keeps only its verb word (22:18 ἐξ, 22:24 εἰς); oblique government riding with the governed word where the ASV writes a verb word of its own for the compound (22:11 as corrected, 22:24, 22:26). 22:22 Αἶρε to 'Away with' takes the rule's closing exception. The one supplied-object case (22:13 ἐπιστάς to 'standing by me') has no Greek dative and folds under rule 74, so it does not conflict with 22:11.

Evidence round: the corpus answers the distributive-κατά question decisively for the chapter's reading. All 8 κατά-to-'every' units align the distributive determiner to the preposition, headed on the prepositional word where one is written ('in every' on 'in' at ACT.14.23, ACT.15.21, ACT.20.23, TIT.1.5; 'of every' on 'of' at LUK.8.4) and on 'every' where none is (ACT.8.3, LUK.2.41, JHN.21.25); the arthrous parallel ACT.8.3 does not align its article to 'every', since the article query returns only LUK.21.37, where no preposition competes. 22:19 stands as accepted, and I promoted the principle rather than leave it to be rediscovered.

BSB: none of the ten disagreements is a genuine error. Six are ordinary article displacement or a determinerless article (22:3 τοῦ, 22:8 ὁ, 22:14 τοῦ, 22:19 τὰς, 22:28 τὴν) and a particle the ASV writes no word for (22:28 καί, rule 65). 22:25 Εἰ is an interrogative particle the ASV marks by inversion alone, decided on rules 44 and 64's English-side test. The remaining three are the two chapter judgments now recorded as conventions: compressed appositional ἀνήρ (22:1, 22:3) and collapsed periphrastic εἰμί (22:19). No accepted edge was touched.

The single added unit, 22:28 'a Roman' for the elliptical καὶ γεγέννημαι, is right under rules 5 and 103: γεγέννημαι's English is complete at 'born', the supplied words are a full lexical predicate rather than anything on rule 7's list, and the licensing lexeme Ῥωμαῖος stands in 22:25–29 and in no token of this verse. Rule 37 is not the case, there being no versification difference, and rule 97 is not, the projection lacking nothing.
